name: secure-api-design
description: Design APIs securely with rate limiting, proper CORS, request validation, and protection against common API attacks
author: community
content:
## Secure API Design

APIs are the primary attack surface of modern applications. Secure them by default.

### Rate Limiting
- Rate-limit all endpoints — especially auth, search, and data export
- Use token bucket or sliding window algorithm
- Apply limits per IP, per user, and per API key (layered)
- Return `429 Too Many Requests` with `Retry-After` header
- Rate-limit failed auth attempts more aggressively than normal requests
- Consider different rate limits for different tiers (free vs paid)

### CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing)
- NEVER use `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` for authenticated APIs
- Allowlist specific origins — do not reflect the `Origin` header blindly
- Restrict `Access-Control-Allow-Methods` to only the methods your API uses
- Restrict `Access-Control-Allow-Headers` to required headers only
- Set `Access-Control-Max-Age` to cache preflight responses
- Do not expose sensitive headers via `Access-Control-Expose-Headers`

```javascript
// BAD — open to all origins
app.use(cors());

// GOOD — restrictive
app.use(cors({
  origin: ['https://app.example.com'],
  methods: ['GET', 'POST', 'PUT', 'DELETE'],
  credentials: true,
  maxAge: 86400
}));
```

### Request Validation
- Validate Content-Type header — reject unexpected types
- Enforce maximum request body size
- Validate and sanitize all path parameters, query parameters, and body fields
- Use schema validation (JSON Schema, Zod, Joi, Pydantic) on every endpoint
- Reject requests with unexpected fields (strict schema validation)
- Validate pagination parameters — cap `limit`/`page_size` to prevent data dumping

### Response Security
- Never return more data than the client needs — use field selection or view models
- Strip internal fields (IDs, timestamps, internal flags) unless explicitly needed
- Implement pagination — never return unbounded result sets
- Set security headers on all responses:
  - `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`
  - `X-Frame-Options: DENY`
  - `Cache-Control: no-store` for sensitive data
  - `Content-Security-Policy` appropriate to your needs

### CSRF Protection
- Use anti-CSRF tokens for cookie-based auth (synchronizer token or double-submit cookie)
- Set `SameSite=Lax` or `Strict` on session cookies
- Verify `Origin` and `Referer` headers for state-changing requests
- Token-based auth (Bearer tokens) is inherently CSRF-resistant if tokens are not in cookies

### Mass Assignment Prevention
```python
# BAD — accepts any field the client sends
user.update(**request.json)

# GOOD — explicit allowlist
allowed = {'name', 'email', 'bio'}
data = {k: v for k, v in request.json.items() if k in allowed}
user.update(**data)
```

### API Versioning Security
- Deprecate and remove old API versions — they accumulate unpatched vulnerabilities
- Apply the same security controls to all API versions
- Do not leave debug/test endpoints in production API routes

### GraphQL-Specific
- Implement query depth limiting
- Implement query complexity analysis
- Disable introspection in production
- Rate-limit by query complexity, not just request count
